invariants.avoid: Injecting the service but still calling new on a second helper inside the handler is the same bypass.
invariants.fixHint: Declare the provider as a constructor parameter with private readonly and call it through this.

relations.why: NEST-CTRL-001 tells controllers to receive providers as private readonly constructor parameters, and TS-LEGACY-005 denies constructor parameter properties.
relations.settle: Nest also injects plain constructor parameters: declare the field and assign it in the constructor body to satisfy both, or exclude Nest controllers and providers from TS-LEGACY-005.

source.locator: controllers and providers with constructor injection
source.paraphrase: Controllers handle HTTP and delegate domain work to providers, which the injector supplies through the constructor.

invariants.why: A manually constructed provider skips scope, lifecycle hooks, and test doubles, so the handler runs a different object than the module built.

invariants.avoid: @Get with a name like getCreatedOrders still starts with get, which is a read verb and is fine.
invariants.fixHint: Pair create/update/delete/remove names with @Post/@Put/@Patch/@Delete, or rename the method to what the GET returns.

source.paraphrase: Each route decorator declares the HTTP method. The handler name should read as that operation.

invariants.why: A GET handler named create lies in logs, traces, and generated clients, and reviewers approve a read that writes.

invariants.avoid: Returning an object with a status field is a payload, not this rule. Only res.status(NNN) matches.
invariants.fixHint: Return the value and set @HttpCode(HttpStatus.CREATED), or throw an HttpException built from HttpStatus.

relations.why: NEST-CODE-001 directs error responses to a thrown HttpException, and TS-THROW-001 denies throws inside methods of an exported controller class.
relations.settle: Exclude **/*.controller.ts from TS-THROW-001: Nest maps a thrown HttpException to the response. Keep TS-THROW-001 on services and domain code.

source.paraphrase: Status codes have named enum members. @HttpCode sets the code without touching the response object.

invariants.why: A bare 200 hides whether the author meant OK, and res.status locks the handler to Express instead of the framework reply.

invariants.avoid: A filled @UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard) is the fix, not a second empty decorator on the same handler.
invariants.fixHint: Pass the guard class, for example @UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard), or delete the decorator.

source.paraphrase: Guards decide who reaches a route. @UseGuards takes the guard classes that run before the handler.

invariants.why: An empty @UseGuards() reads as protected in review while enforcing nothing, so the route ships open.

invariants.avoid: @Param() with no key reads the whole params object and needs no pipe. Only a named key without a pipe matches.
invariants.fixHint: Add the pipe inline: @Param("id", ParseIntPipe) id: number, or ParseUUIDPipe for uuid routes.

source.paraphrase: Route values arrive as strings. A pipe such as ParseIntPipe converts and rejects them before the handler.

invariants.why: The route value may intentionally be a string. This check cannot tell when conversion is required.

source.paraphrase: Injecting @Res() or @Response() puts the handler in library-specific mode and disables Nest interceptors and @HttpCode unless { passthrough: true } is passed.

invariants.why: Without { passthrough: true }, Nest stops serializing the return value, skips response interceptors, and hangs if the handler returns a value without manually calling res.send().
invariants.fixHint: Pass @Res({ passthrough: true }) so you can set cookies or headers while letting Nest send the returned value through its standard pipeline.
invariants.avoid: Handlers that legitimately stream a raw response must disable this rule for that route. Options passed through a variable are not evaluated.
